_README: Climate, when-to-go logic, festival calendar and Tet mechanics from DK 2015 pp32–39 and p270. Paraphrase only. Lunar-calendar festivals shift every year: dates here are the book's 2015 approximations and are leads. Our published climate layer (best-time-to-visit-vietnam, geo.ts climate tables) is the published truth; nothing here overrides it.

climate.claim: Three regimes, not one: the SOUTH is warm and humid all year with a May–Oct/Nov wet season; the CENTRAL COAST has typhoons Jul–Nov and its heaviest rain Sep–Dec, with cool rainy winters; the NORTH has cold wet winters Nov–Mar (occasional snow on Fansipan) and hot humid summers wettest May–Aug.
The hot season Feb–Apr can reach about 35°C / 95°F with 80–100% humidity.

The book's own one-line summary ('dry Nov–Feb') is wrong for the central coast, whose wettest month is October–November; its own climate chart shows Hue's October rain exceeding Hanoi's wettest month. Treat any single-country 'dry season' claim as a red flag.

Chart figures (OCR-partial, mm per month for Apr/Jul/Oct/Jan): Hanoi ≈ 81/323/99/20; Hue ≈ 51/72/516+/≈100; Halong Jul ≈ 316; Phan Thiet ≈ 51/295/260/≈0. Cities charted: Lao Cai, Son La, Hanoi, Halong City, Hue, Pleiku, Nha Trang, Quang Ngai, Phan Thiet, Dalat, HCMC, Chau Doc, Can Tho.
climate.verify_against: NCHMF / WMO normals; the site's geo.ts climate layer already holds verified month tables
climate.note: OCR of a graphic; use only as a sanity check, never as a figure.

climate.claim: Mui Ne is windy Oct–Feb (kitesurf season), i.e. its best beach-lounging months are its windiest.

when_to_go.claim: DK's overall pick: March–May for better weather and fewer crowds; Dec–Feb for Tet atmosphere but higher prices; rainy months are off-season and cheaper but bring floods and poor visibility.
when_to_go.note: Decision the book leaves open: it never reconciles 'March–May is best' with the central coast's own calendar or with the north's spring drizzle.

when_to_go.claim: Peak flying season is Dec–Feb because overseas Vietnamese (Viet Kieu) fly home for Christmas and Tet; DK says book flights for that window at least three months ahead, and high-end hotels too; budget rooms rarely sell out.
when_to_go.verify_against: Fare-trend data for SFO/LAX→SGN/HAN around Tet

when_to_go.claim: Domestic flight peak is mid-November to mid-March; reserve ahead.
HCMC and Hanoi hotels can be full of business travellers at any time of year, independent of tourist season.

LP's national seasons: HIGH Jul–Aug (coast prices up to 50% higher, book ahead; hot, humid, summer monsoon everywhere but the far north); SHOULDER Dec–Mar (Tet moves the whole country and raises prices; cool north of Nha Trang, cold in the far north; south clear and sunny); LOW Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov, 'perhaps the best time to tour the whole nation', with typhoons on the central and northern coast until November.
when_to_go.note: LP adds Sep–Nov to DK's Mar–May verdict; neither resolves the central coast's autumn rain inside that window.

when_to_go.claim: LP's month verdicts distilled: April 'generally excellent' nationwide; May fine for centre and north, quiet; June good just before domestic peak but humid; August the PEAK month for domestic and foreign tourism — book everything; September 'excellent' nationwide, coast quieter; October good in the far north, winter rain starts in the centre, south often dry; December quiet until mid-month then resorts fill for Christmas.

Per-city 'when to go' from LP's region openers: Hanoi Oct–Dec ideal, Jun–Aug low season; Hue/central May and September, avoid Oct–Jan; Nha Trang July, Mui Ne December for wind; Dalat October; HCMC Feb–Mar driest, December cooler; Phu Quoc January. Put together, there is no month that is best everywhere, which is the planner's whole problem.
Book accommodation a day or two ahead normally, several weeks ahead for Tet, July–August and Christmas; pre-book internal flights and trains; Tet flights are hard to get at all.

Activity seasons: surf and kitesurf peak Nov–Apr with the winter monsoon (Mui Ne mornings for beginners, 35-knot afternoons); dive visibility best Jun–Aug and poor Nov–Apr; do not attempt Fansipan May–Sep; Cat Tien best in cooler December.

tet.claim: Tet Nguyen Dan, the lunar new year, is the one festival that matters. The week before: debts settled, graves cleaned, homes decorated with peach blossom (north) or kumquat trees, Kitchen God offerings, flower markets everywhere. The three core days are domestic: families at home, ancestors believed to visit, paper offerings burned.
Officially a three-day holiday, but businesses often shut for a week; some shops close for days, others open late.
tet.verify_against: Current Labour Code public-holiday schedule (Tet is now 5 days off plus weekends, typically 7–9 days)

tet.claim: Firecrackers have been banned since 1994, down to playing recordings; paper firecracker garlands are paraded instead.
tet.verify_against: Decree 137/2020/ND-CP (legalised certain non-explosive 'fireworks' for private use from 2021); state fireworks displays happen

tet.claim: Tet foods: banh chung / banh tet sticky-rice cakes, chicken, dried fruit, watermelon. Human chess is played only at Tet; lion/unicorn dances.
The Vietnamese zodiac has a Cat where China has a Rabbit; years cycle in 12 within 60-year hoi. 2026 is a Horse year.

LP's Tet box: falls between 19 January and 20 February; three official days but most take the week; rites start seven days before (altars, graves visited, absent family return); debts paid and cleaning 'the national sport'; a kumquat, peach or apricot New Year tree; maximum noise at midnight; New Year's Day conduct sets the year — no anger, sweeping, sewing, swearing or breaking things.

The first visitor to a household on New Year's Day is believed to set its luck (a wealthy married father is ideal) — LP notes foreigners may not be considered auspicious. Etiquette: do not be the first through a Vietnamese family's door on Tet morning unless invited for that purpose.
Around Tet shops close and 'virtually all transport ceases'; trains run a bare-bones schedule with most services suspended for nine days, four before to four after Tet; buses and flights sell out.

festival_calendar._note: Lunar months unless marked fixed. Each entry is a lead for the specific date; the existence and character of the festival is context.

lunar_month_1.claim: Communist Party founding day, Feb 3 (fixed; not a day off).
Tay Son festival, Binh Dinh, early Feb: elephants, drumming, martial arts, a week long.
Yen Tu pilgrimage season mid-Feb to end April (Truc Lam Buddhism's founding mountain).
Lim festival, Bac Ninh, 14 days after Tet: quan ho call-and-response courtship singing, wrestling, weaving contests.
Perfume Pagoda festival runs about three months, Feb–May; thousands of pilgrims.

lunar_month_2.claim: Trung Sisters festival, Hanoi, early March: statues carried to the Red River for a ritual bath.
Ba Chua Kho temple, Bac Ninh, March: worshippers symbolically borrow money from the goddess for the year.

lunar_month_3.claim: Thay Pagoda festival, early April: water-puppet shows for the art's patron saint.
Hon Chen temple, Hue: boat procession on the Perfume River in the 3rd and 7th lunar months.
Thanh Minh grave-tending day, early April, nationwide.
Hung Kings' festival, Phu Tho, 10th day of the 3rd lunar month, three days, public holiday.
Liberation/Reunification Day, April 30 (fixed), marks the fall of Saigon; followed by May 1 Labour Day — together a long weekend with heavy domestic travel.
Danang International Fireworks Festival — LP has it in the last week of April; it now runs over several weekends from late spring into summer.
Hue Festival was biennial (2016, 2018) with most performances inside the citadel; since 2022 it runs as a year-round four-season programme.

lunar_month_4_5.claim: Ho Chi Minh's birthday May 19 (fixed; quasi-spiritual; not a day off).
Buddha's birthday (Le Phat Dan), 15th of the 4th lunar month: lanterns at temples and homes.
Tet Doan Ngo, 5th day of the 5th month: summer-solstice 'kill the inner insects' festival.
Nha Trang Sea Festival at the end of May / start of June (street festival, kites, exhibitions); biennial.
Quang Trung festival at Dong Da mound, Hanoi, on the 5th day of the first lunar month: wrestling, lion dances, human chess.
Saigon Cyclo Challenge, a charity race of cyclo drivers in HCMC each March.
Buon Ma Thuot Coffee Festival in March (biennial, odd years).

lunar_month_7_8.claim: Trung Nguyen / Vu Lan, mid-7th lunar month (Aug): 'wandering souls' day, the most important festival after Tet; paper money burned for the dead.
National Day Sep 2 (fixed): parades in Ba Dinh Square, Hanoi.
Do Son buffalo fighting, Haiphong, early Sep; the animals are slaughtered afterwards, which many Western readers will want to know before going.
Mid-Autumn / Children's Moon Festival, 15th of the 8th month (mid-Sep): lanterns, masks, moon cakes; Hang Ma street in Hanoi is the hub.
Whale festival, Phan Thiet, Sep: whale veneration of Cham/Khmer origin.

lunar_month_9_12.claim: Kate, the Cham new year, Sep–Oct at Po Klong Garai towers near Phan Rang; follows the Cham calendar.
Keo Pagoda festival, Thai Binh, mid-Oct, three days.
Confucius' birthday is observed as Teachers' Day (modern VN: Nov 20).
Oc Om Boc and ngo boat races, Soc Trang, mid-Nov: Khmer moon festival, canoes carved from single trees, crews from Vietnam and Cambodia.

lunar_month_9_12.verify_against: Now biennial (odd years, e.g. Dec 2025, Dec 2027)

lunar_month_9_12.claim: Christmas is celebrated enthusiastically in the big cities (lights, fake snow) given the large Catholic population; Jan 1 is a holiday but minor.
Christmas is not a holiday but is celebrated enthusiastically; LP singles out Phat Diem cathedral (Ninh Binh) and HCMC midnight Mass; from mid-December resorts fill — book Christmas rooms well ahead.
Oc Om Boc boat races on the 15th of the 10th moon (late Oct or Nov) at Ba Dong beach (Tra Vinh) and on the Soc Trang river.

public_holidays_2015.claim: 2015 list: Jan 1; Tet 3 days; Hung Kings; Apr 30; May 1; Sep 2. (Feb 3 and May 19 are commemorations, not days off.)
public_holidays_2015.verify_against: Current list adds a second day at National Day (Sep 1 or 3) and gives Tet 5 days; verify annually via the government's published holiday schedule

seasonal_hooks.claim: Autumn (Aug–Oct) is when the north turns cool and pleasant and is the best season to follow northern festivals; winter (Nov–Jan) is cold and drizzly in the north with few festivals.
Spring (Feb–Apr) is the most festive season nationally, and the Red River Delta has the densest festival calendar.
Bach Ma NP's Rhododendron Trail flowers in spring.

LP's 2016 public-holiday list matches DK's; it also lists Buddha's birthday as a holiday on the 8th of the 4th moon, which is wrong on both counts (the date is the 15th and it is not a public holiday).
